research_rationale: EO 10358 of June 9, 1952 (official text 17 FR 5269, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line) sets holiday-observance rules for executive agencies: application (s.1), definitions of holiday and workday (s.2), closing of offices on the Monday after a Sunday holiday (s.3), next-workday and in-lieu rules for employees (ss.4-6), pay-and-leave treatment (s.7), and an effective date sixty days after signing with supersession of EO 9636 (s.8). EO 11226 (May 27, 1965, 30 FR 7213) rewrote section 7 and added a section 9 for employees on uncommon tours of duty, effective on issuance; EO 11272 (February 23, 1966, 31 FR 3111) rewrote section 1 and added a section 10 excluding the postal field service from sections 4-7 and 9, effective on issuance. These amendments modified but did not end any original clause (each rewritten clause kept its original rule), so they are recorded as later events, not first ends. EO 11582 of February 11, 1971 (36 FR 2957, read in full) section 8 revokes EO 10358 and the amendatory EOs 11226 and 11272, and section 9 makes the order 'effective as of January 1, 1971', so the revocation is effective 1971-01-01 (the same day the Monday-holiday statute moved several of the dates listed in section 2(a); nothing ended any clause earlier). The order has no expiry or condition. The eCFR conflict lead (7 CFR 800.0 still mentions 'Executive Order 10358, as amended' when explaining weekend holiday observance) was read: it is a stale descriptive cross-reference in a grain-inspection definition and cannot keep a revoked order operating; the operative rules are 5 U.S.C. 6103 and EO 11582, so the lead is resolved and does not contradict the NO status. Section 8 is inventoried in two quoted parts because the OCR fuses the footnote marker to the superseded order's number (the number would not be a valid order number as printed); the omitted token is the number of EO 9636, identified by its date and title. All clauses first ended 1971-01-01, which is the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text and have not been compared with page images.

research_rationale: EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled "Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions."' research_rationale: EO 9767 of August 9, 1946 (official text 11 FR 8710, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line; its last line is printed on the next page after a fragment of another document, so paragraph (d) is inventoried in two parts) amends the Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees (section V-15 of the Foreign Service Regulations, EO 7968 as amended): (a) rewrites the last sub-item of Item 6 (certified copy of a repatriation form under the Nationality Act of 1940), (b) revokes the first exception under Item 24, (c) and (d) rewrite the second and third exceptions under Item 24 (no-fee oaths of allegiance under the 1940 Act). EO 10473 of July 22, 1953 (18 FR 4351, read in full) section 4(b)(3) amends 'The last item' of Item 6 to the Immigration and Nationality Act repatriation form, section 4(d)(1) revokes 'The first item under the word Exceptions' of Item 24 and section 4(d)(3) amends 'The last item appearing under the word Exceptions', each 'effective as of December 24, 1952'. No amendatory order intervened between 1946 and 1953 (EO 10697 section 7 lists the whole chain: 7968, 8297, 9303, 9407, 9507, 9591, 9767, 10473, 10639), so after EO 9767 revoked the first exception its (c) item was the first item and its (d) item the last; the successor texts match them item for item (same subjects, with the 1952 Act substituted). Those three clauses therefore first ended 1952-12-24. The opening amending clause and the revocation in (b) stayed in force until EO 10697 of February 6, 1957 (22 FR 777, read in full), which prescribed a new Tariff of Fees and in section 7 revoked EO 9767 'To the extent that they have not heretofore been revoked or superseded', effective March 1, 1957 (section 8).
